name: Cruz NDO
question: Does intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U or 300 U reduce urinary incontinence compared with placebo in neurogenic detrusor overactivity?

design.population: 275 adults aged 18-80 with multiple sclerosis (154) or spinal cord injury (121), neurogenic detrusor overactivity, at least 14 urinary incontinence episodes per week, and inadequate response or intolerance to anticholinergics.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Study participants, p 743; Table 1, p 745

verdictNote: Both doses improved the week-6 primary endpoint; 300 U offered no clinically relevant efficacy gain.
takeaway: In patients with multiple sclerosis or spinal cord injury and neurogenic detrusor overactivity, intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U and 300 U reduced weekly incontinence episodes at week 6 by 21.8 and 19.4 versus 13.2 with placebo (each P < 0.01).

reports.label: Phase 3 primary report
reports.citation: Cruz F, Herschorn S, Aliotta P, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA in Patients with Urinary Incontinence Due to Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity: A Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial." *Eur Urol.* 2011;60(4):742-750. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2011.07.002
reports.followUp: Week 6 primary assessment; first treatment cycle followed for up to 52 weeks

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in weekly urinary incontinence episodes at week 6
results.note: Intent-to-treat (all 275 randomized); last observation carried forward for weekly incontinence change. ANCOVA compared each dose with placebo at two-sided alpha 0.025.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 743; Table 2 and footnotes, p 746

results.measure: No urinary incontinence episodes during week 6
results.note: Intent-to-treat responder analysis; counts inferred from rounded percentages and randomized arm sizes.
results.locator: Full text, Primary efficacy end point, p 745; Figure 2B, pp 745-746

results.note: Week-6 change from baseline in the intent-to-treat population; urodynamics performed at week 6.

results.endpoint: Maximum detrusor pressure at first involuntary contraction
results.note: Week-6 change among patients with an involuntary detrusor contraction; arm-specific measured denominators were not printed.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and footnote d, p 746

results.measure: Change in I-QOL total score at week 6
results.note: I-QOL improved more with both doses than placebo at week 6; numerical values appear only in Figure 3A.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Figure 3A, pp 745-746

results.measure: Median time to patient request for retreatment
results.note: Kaplan-Meier time to patient request for retreatment; request permitted from week 12 when weekly incontinence reduction was below 30%.
results.locator: Full text, Study design, p 743; Results and Figure 4, pp 745-746

harms.label: Clean intermittent catheterization initiated after treatment among patients not using it at baseline
harms.note: Safety population among baseline nonusers of CIC; counts calculated from Table 6 percentages and group denominators, across treatment cycle 1.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection and urinary retention during the first 12 weeks
harms.note: Safety population (treated patients). UTI included positive urine cultures without symptoms; retention was investigator-defined.
harms.locator: Full text, Safety evaluations, p 743; Table 5, p 748

harms.label: Serious adverse events and autonomic dysreflexia during treatment cycle 1
harms.value: 37/270 treated patients had at least one serious adverse event; one treatment-related event was muscular weakness in the 300-U group. Two SCI patients experienced autonomic dysreflexia, one in each active-dose group.
harms.locator: Full text, Safety and tolerability, p 746
harms.note: No Clavien-Dindo grading or reoperation counts were reported.

delivery.label: Injection pattern
delivery.value: OnabotulinumtoxinA 200 U, 300 U, or placebo was delivered cystoscopically in 30 intradetrusor 1-mL injections approximately 1 cm apart and 2 mm deep, sparing the trigone; injections were performed without anesthesia, after bladder local anesthesia, or under general anesthesia as needed.

delivery.label: Early response
delivery.value: An active-treatment benefit was observed at the first posttreatment visit, week 2; repeat treatment could be requested from week 12 if weekly incontinence episodes had fallen by less than 30% from baseline.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study design, p 743; Primary efficacy end point, p 745

delivery.label: First-cycle completion and retreatment
delivery.value: 230/275 randomized patients (83.6%) completed placebo-controlled cycle 1; 5/275 (1.8%) discontinued because of adverse events. Of 137 retreated patients, 74 received the same active dose again.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 744; Figure 1, p 744

reports.label: Pooled four-year extension
reports.citation: Kennelly M, Dmochowski R, Schulte-Baukloh H, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA Therapy Are Sustained Over 4 Years of Treatment in Patients With Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity: Final Results of a Long-Term Extension Study." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2017;36(2):368-375. doi:10.1002/nau.22934
reports.followUp: Mean 3.6 years in 388 treated patients pooled from two phase 3 trials

results.measure: Mean change from study baseline in episodes/day at week 6 across six 200-U treatment cycles
results.note: Pooled treated population; descriptive analysis without a prespecified statistical threshold or randomized placebo comparison.
results.locator: Full text, Study Assessments and Statistical Analyses, p 369; Results and Figure 2A, pp 370-372

results.measure: Overall median time to retreatment request among 200-U-only patients with completed treatment cycles
Mean I-QOL increase across six 200-U treatment cycles
results.note: The minimally important difference was 11 points.
results.locator: Full text, Efficacy Measures and Figure 3A, pp 371-373

harms.label: New clean intermittent catheterization among prior nonusers by dose and treatment cycle

values.u200: 26/88 (29.5%) after cycle 1; 2/58 (3.4%) after cycle 2; 3/50 (6.0%) after cycle 3
values.u300: 43.0% after cycle 1; 15.0% after cycle 2; 4.8% after cycle 3

harms.note: Pooled extension population from the two phase 3 trials.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection and urinary retention after first treatment
harms.note: Events within 12 weeks of the first onabotulinumtoxinA treatment in the pooled treated population.

harms.label: Neutralizing-antibody seroconversion during extension
harms.value: 8/381 (2.1%) overall; 3/200 (1.5%) among patients receiving the approved 200-U dose.

delivery.label: Extension eligibility and retention
delivery.value: 396 patients entered the extension after completing either phase 3 trial; 388 received onabotulinumtoxinA and 240/396 (60.6%) were followed for at least four years.

delivery.label: Repeat-treatment protocol
delivery.value: Initially 200 U or 300 U via 30 cystoscopic 1-mL trigone-sparing detrusor injections; after a 2011 amendment, all received 200 U. Retreatment required patient request, at least 12 weeks since injection, and at least one incontinence episode in three days.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Design and Participants, p 369

reports.label: Four-year completers
reports.citation: Rovner E, Kohan A, Chartier-Kastler E, et al. "Long-Term Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA in Patients with Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity Who Completed 4 Years of Treatment." *J Urol.* 2016;196(3):801-808. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2016.04.046
reports.followUp: Four years among 227 completers from the pooled trials

results.measure: Week-6 mean reduction in episodes/day across four treatment years

values.u200: -3.4, -3.6, -3.8, -3.7 episodes/day in years 1-4 (200-U-only cohort, n=122 completers)
values.u300: -3.6, -3.4, -3.8, -3.9 episodes/day in years 1-4 (300/200-U cohort, n=105 completers)

results.note: Post-hoc descriptive analysis of 227 four-year completers; pooled year-1 to year-4 changes were -3.5, -3.5, -3.8, and -3.8 episodes/day. Year-specific denominators were not printed in Figure 3.
results.locator: Full text, Study Outcomes, p 802; Statistical Analyses, p 803; Figure 3, p 805

results.measure: 100% reduction in daily incontinence episodes at week 6, across treatment years
results.note: Among four-year completers treated in a given year; pooled rates were 46.3%, 51.7%, 53.2%, and 52.0% in years 1-4. Year-specific denominators were not printed in Figure 4B.

results.measure: Mean change from phase-3 baseline at week 6 after treatment by year among four-year completers

values.u200: +29.4, +31.7, +31.1, +29.5 points in years 1-4 (200-U-only cohort, n=122 completers)
values.u300: +34.4, +29.7, +34.0, +33.8 points in years 1-4 (300/200-U cohort, n=105 completers)

results.note: Pooled changes were +31.7, +30.8, +32.2, and +31.4 points in years 1-4; the minimally important difference was 11 points. Year-specific denominators were not printed in Figure 5.

results.measure: Median time from injection to patient request for retreatment among completers with completed cycles
results.locator: Full text, Results and Figure 2, p 804

harms.label: De novo catheterization among patients who had never used CIC at start of year
harms.note: Pooled 37/85 (43.5%) initiated CIC in year 1 and 0/36 in year 4; denominators are completers who had never used CIC at the start of each year.

harms.label: Urinary infection and retention within 12 weeks of treatments in four-year completers
harms.value: UTI: 73/340 treatments (21.5%) in year 1 and 43/228 (18.9%) in year 4; retention: 45/340 (13.2%) in year 1 and 7/228 (3.1%) in year 4. UTI did not require symptoms; retention was investigator-defined.
harms.locator: Full text, Study Outcomes, p 802; Table 2, p 806

delivery.label: Four-year completion and treatment frequency
delivery.value: 227/388 (58.5%) treated patients completed four years; completers received a mean 1.4-1.5 treatments per year.
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 1, p 803; Results and Figure 1, pp 803-804

relations.note: Independent phase 3 replicate in the same NDO program; both cohorts fed the pooled long-term extension.
